question: Should OpenClaw add a public per-target-agent subagent concurrency cap under `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent`, and how should it compose with global and requester-session limits?
rationale: This adds a compatibility-sensitive configuration contract and scheduling policy; automation cannot safely choose the permanent namespace or hierarchical admission semantics.

options.title: Nested target cap
options.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` and enforce keyed target admission within the existing global subagent safety cap.

options.title: Top-level agent cap
options.body: Add `agents.list[].maxConcurrent`, accepting ambiguity with top-level inbound agent concurrency.

options.title: Keep current controls
options.body: Decline a new config surface and rely on global and requester-session limits plus operational separation.

recommendation.title: Nested target cap
recommendation.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` and enforce keyed target admission within the existing global subagent safety cap.

likelyOwner.reason: The central concurrency resolver, lane setup, dominant file history, and prior issue review most strongly connect this person to the decision.
